zps.ponder.cable.text_1: Cables don't do anything on their own.
zps.ponder.cable.text_2: Add Redstone Converters to send a redstone signal.
zps.ponder.energy.text_1: Stepup Transformers draw FE from their adjacent block...
zps.ponder.energy.text_2: ...and deposit the FE to connected Stepdown Transformers.
zps.ponder.energy_explode.text_1: Be careful not to supply FE to a Redstone Converter...
zps.ponder.energy_explode.text_2: Redstone Converters cannot handle the higher voltage, and will explode.
zps.ponder.insulation.text_1: Bare cables will always connect, and sometimes this is not wanted.
zps.ponder.insulation.text_2: Apply Insulation to prevent cable blocks from making new connections.
zps.ponder.dense_cables.text_2: Dense Cables can transmit 4 signals through a single block.
zps.ponder.dense_cables.text_3: Use Dense Cable Separators to merge multiple regular cables into a Dense Cable.
zps.ponder.dense_cables.text_4: Dense Cable Separators can be rotated with Shift + R-Click
zps.ponder.octo_controller.text_1: Interact with an Octo-Controller to control it.
zps.ponder.octo_controller.text_2: By default, WASD and Space, Q, Left Shift and E control the 8 redstone outputs.
zps.ponder.octo_controller.text_3: Interact with the controller again to step off.
zps.ponder.octo_controller.text_4: Sneak and interact with an empty hand to choose the key for each output.
zps.ponder.data_cable.text_1: Data Cables send information as text between compatible blocks.
zps.ponder.data_cable.text_2: A minimum setup has an input and output.
zps.ponder.data_cable.text_3: Data provided to the input is sent to all connected outputs.
zps.ponder.script_terminal.text_1: The Script Terminal sends commands to interact with other blocks, through connected Serial Busses.
zps.ponder.script_terminal.text_2: To input commands, interact with the Script terminal to open a GUI.
zps.ponder.script_terminal.text_3: When given a Redstone signal, the Script Terminal will dispatch each of its commands, in sequence.
zps.ponder.script_terminal.text_4: Each command is executed once for each connected Serial Bus, positioned in front of the Serial Bus interface.
zps.ponder.data_transcriber.text_1: The Data Transcriber can write Data to a Book and Quill held in a Lectern or Data Lectern underneath.
zps.ponder.data_transcriber.text_2: When powered, it will copy the input Data to the current page of the book below.
zps.ponder.data_transcriber.text_3: If the input Data changes while the Data Transcriber is powered, it will turn to the next page and then write the new Data.
zps.ponder.launch_platform.text_1: Launch Platforms turn what is built on them into a ship.
zps.ponder.launch_platform.text_2: A tower of upright Space Truss beside the platforms sets how tall the ship can be.
zps.ponder.launch_platform.text_3: Sneak and look at a platform to see what will be launched.
zps.ponder.launch_platform.text_4: Power a platform with redstone to launch.
zps.ponder.robotic_arm.text_1: The Robotic Arm can interact with and move items between nearby blocks.
zps.ponder.robotic_arm.text_2: While active, the arm consumes 8 FE per tick.
zps.ponder.robotic_arm.text_3: To control the Robotic Arm, send instructions from an adjacent Serial Bus.
zps.ponder.robotic_arm.text_4: The arm can accept a new instruction once every 16 gameticks.
zps.ponder.reactor_intro.text_1: The Fusion Reactor produces large amounts of FE by reacting Flux into Aether.
zps.ponder.reactor_intro.text_2: A Fusion Reactor is a sealed chamber, built out of Reinforced Plating and Reinforced Glass.
zps.ponder.reactor_intro.text_3: The inside of the chamber stays empty, and only holds gas.
zps.ponder.reactor_intro.text_4: Once the chamber is fully sealed, the blocks form a reactor. No controller block is needed.
zps.ponder.reactor_intro.text_5: Reactor Ports move gas through the wall, and can be set to Input or Output.
zps.ponder.reactor_intro.text_6: A Reactor Port stays closed until it receives a Redstone signal, and opens further as the signal gets stronger...
zps.ponder.reactor_intro.text_7: ...until at full strength, the port is fully open.
zps.ponder.reactor_intro.text_8: Heat Exchangers convert FE into heat inside the chamber, or heat back into FE.
zps.ponder.reactor_intro.text_9: Flux enters through an Input port when the Gas Duct's pressure is higher than the chamber's.
zps.ponder.reactor_intro.text_10: Flux has to be heated before it will react.
zps.ponder.reactor_intro.text_11: FE supplied to a Heat Exchanger will heat the gas in the chamber...
zps.ponder.reactor_intro.text_12: ...and at 50,000 K, the Flux fuses into Aether, releasing a large amount of heat.
zps.ponder.reactor_intro.text_13: Once ignited, the reaction keeps the chamber hot by itself.
zps.ponder.reactor_intro.text_14: Heat Exchangers that are not being supplied with FE will generate FE from the chamber's heat.
zps.ponder.reactor_intro.text_15: Aether builds up in the chamber as the Flux reacts. Too much of it will pause the reaction.
zps.ponder.reactor_intro.text_16: An Output port can pump the Aether out. Block Flux in its filter, so that the fuel stays inside.
zps.ponder.reactor_intro.text_17: The reactor keeps running while Flux is supplied and Aether is removed. If the chamber gets too cold, the reaction will stop.
zps.ponder.reactor_monitoring.text_1: A Serial Bus in Get mode can read the state of a reactor from any of its wall blocks.
zps.ponder.reactor_monitoring.text_5: Pressure is read in Pa, temperature in K, and output in FE per tick.
zps.ponder.reactor_monitoring.text_6: Watching these values makes it easier to understand what the reactor is doing, and to avoid a failure.
zps.ponder.reactor_overheating.header: Keeping a Fusion Reactor from Overheating
zps.ponder.reactor_overheating.text_1: A Fusion Reactor will melt one of its wall blocks if the chamber exceeds 200,000 K.
zps.ponder.reactor_overheating.text_2: The chamber heats up whenever the reaction generates heat faster than the Heat Exchangers can remove it.
zps.ponder.reactor_overheating.text_3: The reaction pauses while Aether is above a quarter of the gas, so the Output port sets how fast it can run.
zps.ponder.reactor_overheating.text_4: Weakening the Output port's Redstone signal keeps more Aether inside, so less heat is generated and the Heat Exchangers can catch up.
zps.ponder.reactor_overheating.text_5: A Heat Exchanger can only extract heat while its FE has somewhere to go...
zps.ponder.reactor_overheating.text_6: ...so if the machines it powers are full, it will stop cooling the chamber.
zps.ponder.reactor_overheating.text_7: Each Heat Exchanger can only extract so much heat, so they limit how fast a reactor can safely run.
zps.ponder.reactor_overheating.text_8: To produce more FE, add more Heat Exchangers, then open the Output port further. This will also consume more Flux.
zps.ponder.reactor_bursting.header: Keeping a Fusion Reactor from Bursting
zps.ponder.reactor_bursting.text_1: A Fusion Reactor will burst if the pressure in its chamber exceeds 24 MPa.
zps.ponder.reactor_bursting.text_2: The pressure in the chamber rises and falls with its temperature.
zps.ponder.reactor_bursting.text_3: A chamber filled with cold Flux will reach over a hundred times its pressure by the time it ignites...
zps.ponder.reactor_bursting.text_4: ...and will burst long before it gets there.
zps.ponder.reactor_bursting.text_5: Before igniting, give the Input port only a weak Redstone signal, so that only a little Flux gets in.
zps.ponder.reactor_bursting.text_6: Once the reactor is lit, the Input port can be opened up again.
zps.ponder.reactor_bursting.text_7: A reactor that overheats gains pressure as well, and can burst before its walls melt.
zps.ponder.gas_duct.text_1: Gas Ducts carry gas between blocks.
zps.ponder.gas_duct.text_2: Gas is simulated with a pressure and a temperature. It flows from higher pressure to lower pressure, so it spreads out along the run.
zps.ponder.gas_duct.text_3: Each gas has its own density and heat capacity, so different gases behave differently in the same duct.
zps.ponder.gas_duct.text_4: A Gas Gauge reads the pressure of the gas in the duct it is attached to.
zps.ponder.gas_duct.text_5: Sneak and click it to read temperature instead.
zps.ponder.gas_duct.text_6: A Gas Duct bursts above 16.4 MPa, and is destroyed above 1,478 K.
zps.ponder.gas_duct.text_7: The dial covers exactly this range. A needle at the top of the dial is a duct at its limit.
zps.ponder.gas_duct.text_8: As gas keeps arriving with nowhere to go, the pressure climbs until a duct bursts.
zps.ponder.gas_duct.text_9: A burst leaves the ducts around it open, and they bleed gas into the air until a Gas Duct is placed back against them.
zps.ponder.gas_duct.text_10: A Vent at the end of the run releases gas into the air, so the pressure never reaches the limit.
zps.ponder.tag.can_insulate.description: Components or Blocks which can have Cable Insulation applied to them, which prevents the block from connecting in new directions.
zps.ponder.tag.cable_components.descript: Blocks that carry or use cable signals.
zps.ponder.tag.data_cable_components.des: Blocks that send or receive messages through Data Cables.
zps.ponder.tag.has_script_caps.descripti: Blocks which have extra Script Capabilities beyond the default 'set_redstone' command.
zps.ponder.tag.reactor_wall_blocks.descr: Blocks which can form part of the sealed chamber of a Fusion Reactor.
block.zps.switch_panel.zps_tooltip:
4 levers in 1!

Each switch controls one of the four outputs. Connects with [Dense Cables].
block.zps.graduated_lever.zps_tooltip:
Allows precise control of a redstone signal.

Interact with the upper or lower half of the block to increase or decrease signal strength. Connects with [Cable].
block.zps.power_cell.zps_tooltip:
Stores up to 2.1M FE per cell.

Cells placed in a square column (up to 3x3 wide and 32 tall) join into one larger cell with the combined capacity.

Can be used to charge items that have [Energy Storage].
block.zps.beam_collector.zps_tooltip:
Projects a beam that pulls in items, mobs and blocks. Items and blocks that reach it are stored inside.

Place blocks facing the same way in a square (up to 3x3) to form a larger panel with a longer beam and more storage.

Runs only when receiving a Redstone signal, and consumes FE while running. The signal strength sets the beam's range.
block.zps.coal_burner.zps_tooltip: Burns furnace fuel to generate %s FE/tick.
block.zps.rolling_mill.zps_tooltip:
Consumes FE to roll metal.

Rolls ingots into rods and nuggets into wire.
block.zps.vaporizer.zps_tooltip:
Consumes FE to heat up, then vaporizes items into gas.

Each recipe needs a minimum temperature and cools the machine when it runs. The gas collects in an internal buffer and leaves through the top.
block.zps.air_compressor.zps_tooltip:
Consumes 32 FE/tick to draw gas from the environment through the fan on top.

Turns off when receiving a redstone signal.
block.zps.thruster.zps_tooltip:
Consumes [gas] to push the ship it's on.

See the JEI category for fuel properties.

Activates with a redstone signal.
block.zps.vent.zps_tooltip:
Releases gas from a [Gas Duct] into the air to prevent pressure buildup.

Closes when receiving a redstone signal.

[R-Click] an open vent to climb inside.
Entering a vent with very hot or very cold gas can be dangerous.
block.zps.assembler.zps_tooltip:
Consumes FE to craft items in a [5x5 crafting grid].

Consumes 16 FE/t while crafting, and works only when receiving a Redstone signal.
block.zps.impact_piston.zps_tooltip:
Consumes FE to slam a heavy rod into the block underneath.

Consumes 64 FE/t while raising the rod, and works only when receiving a Redstone signal.
block.zps.sieve.zps_tooltip:
Allows players and mobs to stand on top, while other entities fall through.

Falling blocks that drop through are [sifted]: any loot buried inside is collected in the sieve.
block.zps.catwalk.zps_tooltip: Can be placed on cable blocks to prevent upwards connection.
block.zps.space_grating_block.zps_toolti: Can be placed on cable blocks to prevent connection in new directions.
item.zps.script_book.zps_tooltip: Can also be opened from the Script Terminal screen without this book
block.zps.radio_transmitter.zps_tooltip:
Transmits a radio signal with data from a [Data Cable].

Tune the radio frequency with [Shift + Right Click]. Higher frequencies have a longer range and require a taller [Radio Antenna] on top.
block.zps.radio_receiver.zps_tooltip:
Receives a radio signal and sends the data over a [Data Cable].

Tune the radio frequency with [Shift + Right Click]. Higher frequencies have a longer range and require a taller [Radio Antenna] on top.
block.zps.loudspeaker.zps_tooltip: Converts messages from a [Data Cable] into spoken audio.
block.zps.data_comparator.zps_tooltip:
Compares signals from two connected [Data Cables] according to the current mode.

[Equals]: provides Redstone power when data from the two inputs match exactly.

[Contains]: provides Redstone power when data from the first input contains the full data from the second.

[Greater Than]: provides Redstone power when both inputs can be parsed as numbers and the first is greater than the second.

[Shift + R-Click] to switch Modes.
block.zps.data_combinator.zps_tooltip:
Combines two [Data Cable] inputs into one output according to the current mode.

[Back]: output port.
[Left]: Input A. [Right]: Input B.

[Append]: passthrough behavior for single inputs, and appends Input B to Input A when both are present.

[Replace]: passthrough from Input A unless Input B is present and Input A contains [%s], in which case the first occurrence is replaced with Input B.

[Shift + R-Click] to switch Modes.
item.zps.robotic_arm_segment.zps_tooltip:
Used to construct a [Robotic Arm].

[R-Click an Incomplete Arm]: attaches this arm segment to the incomplete robotic arm.
item.zps.address_pad.zps_tooltip:
Saves named block positions as Addresses.

[R-Click a block]: creates a new Address at that position (max 15).

[R-Click the air]: opens GUI to manage saved Addresses.

[R-Click a Script Terminal]: places the Address Pad on the Script Terminal, allowing the Addresses to be used in Script Commands.
